condition: Abdominal wall pain (anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment)
summary: 36-year-old woman with 8 months of well-localised right-sided abdominal pain at a fingertip-sized spot, normal bloods, previous laparoscopy; Carnett's sign positive.

inputs.hpi: Eight months of sharp pain at one spot beside the right edge of the rectus, worse when twisting or sitting up. No fever, bowel change, weight loss or urinary symptoms. Laparoscopic appendicectomy 2 years ago. Two normal ultrasounds.

exam.abdomen: Soft. Pinpoint tenderness lateral to the right rectus at the level of the umbilicus.

guideline.name: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed.
guideline.section: Abdominal pain and tenderness; hernia; lymphadenopathy; liver

guideline.name: Takada T et al. Carnett's sign in chronic abdominal pain

rationale: A positive Carnett's sign points to the abdominal wall rather than a viscus; with chronic, pinpoint pain and normal tests, abdominal-wall pain belongs in the top three.
